newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil, gas oil edge up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil, gas oil edge up.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil and gas oil swaps edged up at midday Thursday, building on a recent mild rebound on firmer crude prices and general belief that the market has bottomed, traders said.
"The market may have bottomed out and sentiment has improved," one trader said in reference to the latest buying interest for physical fuel oil cargoes.
February fuel oil swaps opened firmer to trade at $100.00 per tonne from Wednesday's $96.50 buying number, brokers said.
The market was last quoted at $100.50/$101.50, one broker said with March quoted at $101.50/$103.00 per tonne, up about $3.00 from Wednesday.
The market rebounded after several physical buyers emerged late Wednesday when offers fell to a low of $93.00 per tonne free-on-board Singapore.
One 20,000-tonne cargo traded at this level between a European major and a Dutch trader but other buyers at this level failed to secure any cargoes.
But others said the rebound may be shortlived as supplies remain healthy.
Gas oil swaps also opened firmer with most sellers said sidelined on expectations of further improvements to the early buying numbers, brokers said.
February bids were seen at up to a high of $26.00 per barrel, compared with Wednesday's $25.50/$25.70.
March bids were quoted at $26.20 per barrel, up from Wednesday's $25.80/$26.00 with the February/March contango narrowing to minus 40/20 cents.
